No, Mycobacterium isn't credibly present in this sample.

The report gives the Mycobacterium genus (taxid 1763) only 6 clade reads out of about 4.0 million. About 98.7% of the reads are classified as Eukaryota, which fits a human-only sample. The Mycobacterium reads split between two species:

| Species | Taxid | Clade reads (rank S) |
|---|---|---|
| *M. spongiae* | 886343 | 3 |
| *M. canetti* (in the *M. tuberculosis* complex) | 78331 | 3 |

The largest count for any single species is 3, well below your 10-read minimum. Counts this low in a human-only sample are typical of misclassification or background noise, not a real organism.
